devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four words. Easy to read past. But this short line is the hinge of the whole book.

Everything in Leviticus that instructs, corrects, restricts, or provides begins here — with God speaking. The offerings were not invented by priests. The system was not developed by trial and error. Israel did not sit down and work out how a holy God might be approached. God told them.

That matters enormously for how we read what follows. Chapter 4 is about sin — sin among leaders, sin among the whole community, sin among ordinary people. And God is the one raising the subject. He brings it up before Israel has time to hide it.

We usually experience conviction as something unwelcome. But consider what it means that God speaks about sin at all. A God who did not care would say nothing. A God who had given up on us would let us carry on undisturbed. Speaking is an act of mercy.

The Lord disciplines the one he loves (Heb 12:6). The Spirit convicts because He is at work, not because He is finished with us (Jn 16:8). Whenever God puts His finger on something in your life, that is not rejection. It is God, once again, speaking first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I hear God's conviction as rejection or as care?
2. Is there something God has been raising with me that I have been avoiding?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You speak to me about my sin rather than leaving me alone in it. Give me ears to hear You as a loving Father. Amen.
